origin: Prospective controls proposed after observing the positive E01B validation results, not independent external confirmation.
reference_model: pretrained MOMENT plus all 15 raw statistical features from E01B
bandwidth_control: In each CV training fold, fit BranchScaler on the selected pretrained-reference training samples only, convert transformed features to float64 exactly as SVC, resolve gamma='scale', and use that SAME numeric gamma plus 0.05 and 5.0 for both controls. Repeat on the selected full training subset for the ordinary final RBF refit. Never fit the gamma reference on validation or the full unlabelled training pool.
statistics_control: Only the original 15 raw statistics, StandardScaler fitted inside each training fold, divided by sqrt(15), preserving exactly the original fusion statistics branch. The pretrained reference is used for a training-only scalar bandwidth diagnostic, not per-sample prediction. This is not an independently tuned, foundation-free training baseline.
random_control: Same frozen MOMENT architecture and patch embedding, randomly initialized with seed equal to the data seed; same mask-aware mean pooling, FP32 and BranchScaler. One random initialization per data seed. Forbid MOMENTPipeline/T5Model/T5EncoderModel.from_pretrained during extraction; record cache provenance. No encoder training and no pretrained checkpoint loading.

decision_rules.statistics_comparator: Maximum validation Macro-F1 among parent statistical RF, parent statistical SVM, and new bandwidth-matched statistics control for the same seed/fraction. Deliberately conservative; the combined statistics comparator has a larger effective search budget.

stop_policy: Complete all 16 new conditions regardless of intermediate outcomes. Preserve separate conclusions for kernel/statistics and pretrained-vs-random controls; do not modify grids, thresholds, seeds or fractions.
next_action: Audit and summarize only. No automatic test evaluation or LoRA/full-finetuning launch.
limitations: The reference validation outcomes are already known. Four data splits overlap, and only one random encoder draw is used per split. These are conditional ablations, not proof of universal superiority over all feature engineering or external-data generalization.
